extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility/selection standards for preparing and submitting an application to the EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowship programme, including required documents, mobility rules, selection criteria and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD degree eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent at the start of the fellowship; applicants who already hold a PhD are eligible if they obtained it within the two years preceding the application submission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to the two-year rule are made for career breaks (parental leave: one year extension per child for female scientists; male scientists get an extension for paternal leave of three months per child or total paternal leave taken, whichever is greater), mandatory military/civil service (documentation required), and possibly extraordinary personal circumstances (severe illness, full-time care of an ill family member) on a case-by-case basis. Applicants without a PhD but with equivalent research experience should contact the Fellowship office prior to submission. The Fellowship Office uses the SUBMISSION date to assess eligibility; applicants must request exceptions prior to submission or the application will be deemed ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications requirement (first-author research paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have at least one first (or joint first) author primary research paper accepted for publication or published in an international peer-reviewed journal at the time the application is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For papers 'accepted' but not yet published, an editorial letter proving first (or co-first) authorship must be sent to the Fellowship office before submitting. A first-author preprint with public in-depth peer reviews is sufficient if: (1) posted on recognized preprint server (e.g., arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Zenodo); (2) peer reviews are publicly available online; (3) reviews come from an independent preprint peer review service (e.g., Peer Community In, Review Commons) and provide in-depth expert analysis. Regular peer-reviewer comments pasted by authors or informal online comments are not accepted. EMBO may consider primary research on preprint servers without reviews but a refereed first-author preprint or peer-reviewed publication is still required. Do not list papers submitted/in preparation, non-English papers, conference abstracts; reviews, comments, book chapters, methods-only papers, videos or patents are not considered primary research (except detailed protocol papers that answer a specific biological question). Do NOT indicate journal impact factors or other journal-based metrics (DORA). Publication updates after submission are not allowed unless the application is withdrawn and re-submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobility — change of country required
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must involve a change of country; EMBO Postdoctoral Fellowships are intended to promote international exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules differ by destination category: (a) To work in an EMBC Member State: applicants of any nationality can apply provided there is international mobility. (b) To work in an EMBC/EMBO global partner: applicants are eligible if they move from, are nationals of, and have performed their PhD in an EMBC Member State or EMBC/EMBO global partner. (c) To work in a Non-EMBC Member State: applicants must move from an EMBC Member State, be nationals of an EMBC Member State, and have performed their PhD in an EMBC Member State. A maximum of 30% of fellowships are awarded in the Non-EMBC category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month previous presence rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who have been living or working in the host country for more than six months in the 18 months before submission are generally ineligible to move to that country under the scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility exception: applicants are eligible if they have been living or working for a maximum of six months in that country during the previous 18 months counting back from the submission date. Candidates who already started working at the host laboratory may apply only if they have been working or living in the host country for a maximum of six months at submission; the relevant start date is the date the candidate started in the host laboratory. The Fellowship Office uses the SUBMISSION date for these checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further mobility exclusions (PhD country and prior lab work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants wishing to work in the country in which they officially obtained their PhD are NOT eligible; working again with the candidate’s PhD supervisor or returning to a lab where the candidate has worked for more than six months are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the PhD is officially shared between two institutions in different countries, both countries are excluded. Visits of less than six months to the future supervisor or any other laboratory in the proposed destination country are permitted. Time spent during master studies counts toward the six-month exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research scope — biological/mechanistic focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals must be within EMBO’s scientific scope and be driven by a biological question that explores mechanisms and yields biological insight rather than remaining at a descriptive or observational level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanistic insight may be at molecular, cellular, tissue, organismal, population, or ecosystem level. Applied or clinical work without a clear biological question is not eligible. Projects directly continuing the applicant’s PhD project will not be considered. Technology-development projects are eligible only if they address a fundamental biology question or enable biological discovery (e.g., microscopy, PCR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity and ethics compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All research activities supported must comply with national and institutional research integrity and ethics requirements (e.g., Belmont Report, European Code of Conduct for Research Integrity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may be asked to provide evidence that planned research conforms to relevant host-institution regulations (human material, animal models, embryonic stem cells, etc.). All EMBO Postdoctoral Fellows are required to complete an online course on research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI tools disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are requested to disclose whether AI tools were used in preparing their applications and for what purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EMBO acknowledges the value of AI and human feedback but applicants remain fully and solely responsible for the originality and accuracy of their applications. The policy may be adapted as generative AI develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of one application per candidate per round
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates may only submit one application, for one project, at one host laboratory at each round of selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting multiple applications in the same round is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host laboratory support limit (one application per host per cycle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective from Autumn 2026, a host laboratory may support a maximum of one application per selection cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple candidates indicate the same host laboratory in the same round, the EMBO Fellowship Office will contact the host laboratory to request withdrawal of the exceeding applications. A host laboratory is defined as a single research unit led by a researcher with their own budget and line of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-application policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Re-application is permitted only once and will be considered only if there are substantial changes to the proposal and/or the applicant's CV or a change of host lab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must outline exact changes in the 'Other Funding' section under 'application changes'. All eligibility criteria must be met at time of re-submission. Candidates may re-apply for the next round while a decision is pending only if they would be ineligible after the decision on the first submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial research / applied project eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to work in an industrial research laboratory with the intention to develop new commercial products or procedures will not be considered; industrial or for-profit labs developing basic biological research projects are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects aimed at developing an application, commercial product, process, or device may be considered only if they have a fundamental biology question to be answered (e.g., technology enabling biological discovery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be written in English and no special formatting is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures and tables cannot be included in the application. The online system shows required fields; registration alone does not make the application complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents: reference and acceptance letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications require two reference letters and an acceptance letter from the receiving institute, submitted via the EMBO online application system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One reference letter must be from the PhD supervisor or co-supervisor; none of the reference letters can come from referees in the receiving institute. Reference letters and the acceptance letter must use institutional email addresses (not private). The application can only be completed and submitted when all required information and the letters have been uploaded and the candidate confirms completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission date as eligibility/evaluation reference and change rules after submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The date and time (CET) when candidates successfully submit their application is the reference date for eligibility and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After submission, only changes in address or contact email are permitted without re-opening the application. All other changes, including publication updates, require the office to re-open the application, which will change the submission date to the date when the application is re-submitted and may affect eligibility. Registration for an account is not sufficient; applications completed after 14:00 CE(S)T on the cutoff date enter the next evaluation round. NO EXCEPTIONS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary selection criteria: excellence of candidate, project, host
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary selection criteria applied by the EMBO Fellowship Committee are the scientific excellence of the candidate, the project and the host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships are awarded to candidates, but the committee also considers the proposed project and host laboratory suitability; substantial changes to project or host after award may lead to termination except in extraordinary circumstances (subject to approval).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspects considered when evaluating applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee assesses scientific achievements of the applicant, the project proposal, and the host laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant: scientific contributions, CV, and performance as indicated in reference letters. Project: quality, scope, novelty, biological significance, and coherent/logical presentation. Host lab: suitability for the proposed research and training, and the lab's scientific achievements. Prior collaborations with the host or projects that continue the PhD generally receive lower priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-screening criteria and items reviewed
rubrics_metrics.description: All complete applications are screened for eligibility and then pre-screened by the EMBO office and Fellowship Committee using a condensed application form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-screening reviews: summary of the applicant’s main scientific achievements and publication list; summary and biological significance of the proposed work; justification for choice of host lab; reference and acceptance letters. Typically top 20–25% proceed to the interview stage. Ineligible applicants receive an email explaining why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview stage format and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Second stage interviews are online video calls with an expert interviewer; candidates must give a presentation as part of the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard interview lasts 90 minutes: first 30 minutes the applicant introduces PhD achievements and describes proposed postdoctoral project; following 60 minutes are dedicated to Q&A. Interviews are scheduled at the interviewer's convenience. Grey-zone applicants may be interviewed by the full Fellowship Committee: prepare a 7-minute presentation summarizing current projects and future directions followed by a 10-minute Q&A. Interview reports feed into final committee evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: No individualized feedback policy
rubrics_metrics.description: No feedback will be provided to applicants at any stage of the application process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to the large number of applications (>1,400 per year), committee members cannot include individualized comments; funds are prioritized for additional fellowships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship duration and start dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are awarded for 24 months although shorter durations can be requested; minimum duration is 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful applicants in the Spring round must start between July 1 and Feb 15 of the following year; Autumn round awardees must start between Jan 1 and Aug 15 of the following year. Fellowships can only start on the 1st or the 15th of each month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondments and restriction on working in PhD country
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows can spend up to 20% of the fellowship duration in another institute/country while still being paid by their host institute, but fellows are not allowed to work in the country where they obtained their PhD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondment fraction counts toward total duration; prior mobility exclusions (six-month rule and PhD country restrictions) still apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment contract (EMBC member states) vs stipend (non-member states)
rubrics_metrics.description: In EMBC member states EMBO provides funds to host institutions to cover the cost of a full-time employment contract (employer social contributions, awardee social contributions, taxes, net salary). For EMBC/EMBO global partners and non-member states fellows receive a stipend intended to cover cost of living.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship does not cover bench fees, overheads, consumables or other financial benefits to the host supervisor or institute. Grant rates are country-dependent and not equivalent to gross salary; if host institution regulations cap salaries below provided funds, the host must return the remainder to EMBO. Stipends may be subject to taxation; EMBO cannot advise on national tax regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel, relocation and childcare allowances
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel & relocation allowance is intended to support travel and relocation costs; child-daycare and dependent child allowances are available in certain categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies and current rates are available in the travel and relocation policy. For fellows outside EMBC, child-daycare support up to €2,500 per fellowship year per child (children under six) is permitted and prorated; claimable after completion of first year with childbirth certificate. Dependent child allowances are country-specific; details in stipend rate sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parental leave and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows whose children are born during the fellowship are entitled to extensions equivalent to the time taken as maternity/parental leave at no cost to EMBO, and specific paid parental leave for stipend fellows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For EMBC member states, part of funds cover social contributions so fellows may access the host country's welfare for parental benefits; extension must be requested by the host supervisor before the end of the fellowship. For fellows in EMBC/EMBO global partners, fellows are entitled to 3 months paid parental leave beginning within 6 months of birth and may request an extension equal to the leave; fellows must inform the Fellowship Office of intention to take leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term sick leave extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows who are not allowed to work for extended periods due to sickness and are paid by the host country's social security can request an extension of their fellowship at no cost to EMBO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The extension must be requested by the host supervisor to the EMBO Fellowship office before the end of the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time work policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Part-time work during the fellowship is possible at no additional cost to EMBO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to work part-time must be discussed with the Host Supervisor and the Fellowship Office. Maximum total fellowship duration (full-time plus part-time) must not exceed 36 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-stipendiary fellowship on early termination
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral Fellows who terminate early their paid EMBO Fellowship due to funding from another source may become EMBO Non-Stipendiary Fellows under conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible they must have received at least one month of paid fellowship and must continue working on the same project in the same lab as described in the application. Fellows who terminate early due to change of research project or career trajectory are not eligible. Non-stipendiary Fellows may attend Fellows’ Meetings and, if they held the paid fellowship for at least 6 months, Laboratory Leadership Courses free of charge. It is not possible to directly apply for a non-stipendiary fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits: network and training access
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded fellows have access to the EMBO Fellows’ Network, Fellows’ Meetings, online platform and EMBO Laboratory Leadership and Scientific Skills courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows two–three years after award are invited to annual Fellows’ Meetings. Fellows can register for courses and access resources via the Fellows Online Network; sign-up is exclusively via that platform. Fee waivers for Laboratory Leadership Courses are granted to fellows within 3 years of being awarded if the fellowship has been held for at least 6 months.
